title: Ops Assistant: converging admin utilities & runbook-as-task workflows
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background: Support and SRE teams currently maintain a collection of one-off admin scripts, a set of markdown runbooks, and several disparate automation hooks in Slack and PagerDuty. This creates friction: runbooks are not executed as tasks, auditability for ad-hoc admin work is low, and onboarding for new on-call engineers is slow.

Goal: Build an "Ops Assistant" workflow layer that: 1) exposes approved admin utilities through a unified CLI and web task surface, 2) treats runbook steps as discrete tasks with status/audit logs, and 3) wires lightweight support automation (templated playbooks + safe fallbacks) into the support triage flow. The intent is not to replace the runtime or owner workflows but to significantly reduce manual variance and improve observability for postmortems and audits.

Success criteria / acceptance: 
- Core admin commands (rotate-keys, drain-node, bump-capacity, snapshot-kv) available in ops-assistant CLI and the Console "Runbooks" panel with identical semantics.
- Each runbook step can be converted to a task that records: who started it, parameters used, start/end timestamps, stdout/stderr, and resulting artifacts (PRs, dashboards).
- Integration with Slack/PagerDuty so that a single click can spawn a task in the Ops Assistant and post status updates back to the incident channel.
- Audit log retention for task records (90 days) and exportable CSV for compliance.
- Safety guards: dry-run mode by default for high-risk steps, explicit two-step confirmation for actions with "destructive" label, and automatic rollback where feasible.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Task Schema and Persistence: define a minimal task record (id, runbook_id, step_id, params, created_by, started_at, ended_at, status, artifacts). Store in the existing ops metadata DB via a new table runbook_tasks.
2) Admin Utility Adapters: create thin adapter layer for our existing admin scripts so they can be executed through the runner with structured outputs (exit code, JSON metadata, logs). Adapters provide parameter validation and dry-run semantics.
3) CLI + Console Integration: extend internal "admin-ux-cli" with commands to list/run/replay tasks. Add a Console panel for runbooks where each step maps to a task button and shows live logs.
4) Automation Hooks: implement a lightweight job runner (runbook-runner) that can execute tasks asynchronously on a dedicated infra pool with resource limits and isolation. Add Slack/PagerDuty webhooks to spawn tasks.
5) Safety and RBAC: leverage existing RBAC to gate destructive actions; add a two-person approval flow for critical steps.
6) E2E Tests + Canary: create synthetic incident tests and a canary on a single SRE on-call rotation. Monitor metrics and rollback if error rate or failures exceed thresholds.

Trade-offs / decisions to make:
- We will not attempt full stateful rollback orchestration in v1; instead, we require explicit rollback tasks in runbooks and provide helpers for common rollback actions. Full transactional rollback will be scoped to v2.
- Centralizing admin utilities increases blast radius; mitigations include strict RBAC, canary rollout, and enabling dry-run by default for high-risk actions.
- Persisting logs increases storage and compliance surface; limit retention to 90 days and provide export hooks rather than long-term cold storage in v1.

Progress updates and current status (high level):
- 2026-02-25: Initial architecture design doc created and reviewed by SRE and Security. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ops-assistant-arch (confluence).
- 2026-03-02: Task schema PR opened for db migration (github.com/redwood/ops-metadata/pull/412). Basic table and index added.
- 2026-03-05: Adapter prototype for "drain-node" created; supports dry-run and structured JSON output. PR: github.com/redwood/admin-utils/pull/89.
- 2026-03-09: Early CLI integration complete with list/run/replay commands; added basic authentication flow and audit recording. PR: github.com/redwood/admin-ux-cli/pull/24.
- 2026-03-12: Console panel mockups reviewed by Design; feedback incorporated. Mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/ops-assistant-mockups.

Open implementation tasks (next steps):
- Complete adapters for rotate-keys and snapshot-kv (ENG-17621).
- Implement runbook-runner job isolation and resource caps (ENG-17622).
- Build Slack/PagerDuty webhook adapters and playbook templates.
- Add RBAC checks and two-person approval flow for destructive actions.

Review feedback and follow-ups:
- Design review (2026-03-10): request to surface safety labels prominently and allow "why is this safe" tooltip for each step. Assigned to Lina Morales for copy and final microcopy.
- Security review (2026-03-08): noted KMS key usage for rotate-keys adapter; Security requested a threat model doc and a short risk mitigation checklist prior to canary.
- PM review (2026-03-11): prioritize rotate-keys and drain-node adapters for the first canary; defer snapshot-kv to post-canary.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: accidental misuse of destructive tools. Mitigation: default dry-run, explicit opt-in, RBAC, and two-person approval.
- Risk: noisy audit logs and DB growth. Mitigation: 90-day TTL and CSV export for long-term retention.
- Risk: on-call cognitive load from new tooling. Mitigation: training session and a "lite" mode exposing only safe, low-friction tasks.

Artifacts and links: 
- Architecture doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ops-assistant-arch
- CLI PR: github.com/redwood/admin-ux-cli/pull/24
- Adapter PR (drain-node): github.com/redwood/admin-utils/pull/89
- Mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/ops-assistant-mockups
- Runbook templates (Drive): https://drive.redwood.com/runbooks/templates/ops-assistant-v1
- Incidence test harness (github): github.com/redwood/ops-tests/tree/ops-assistant-canary

Acceptance test checklist for canary: 
- Execute 10 synthetic tasks (mix of dry-run and apply) without errors.
- Ensure audit entries recorded and downloadable.
- Validate Slack notification roundtrip for task start/finish.
- Confirm RBAC blocks destructive action for read-only role.

Next major milestone: canary rollout to SRE rotation starting 2026-03-20 and post-canary review on 2026-04-03.

Contact: Ravi Patel (assignee) for day-to-day implementation questions, Avery Chen as product-engineering lead for prioritization.

Notes: This ticket intentionally scopes the work to tooling and integration for runbook-as-tasks and safe execution; deeper workflow orchestration (long-running sagas, distributed rollback) is offloaded to follow-up epics to keep v1 deliverable in a single sprint cycle.
